title: Context of Scripture
definition: The Context of Scripture is the surrounding passage, book, history, and biblical storyline that help believers understand what God’s Word means.
summary: The Context of Scripture is the surrounding passage, book, history, and biblical storyline that help believers understand what God’s Word means.
christFocus: Jesus fulfilled the whole storyline of Scripture, so reading in context helps believers see how each passage fits within God’s redemptive plan in Christ.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Context helps us listen to Scripture instead of using Scripture. A verse has words around it, a book it belongs to, an original audience, and a place in the larger story of God’s redemption. Ignoring context often leads to confusion and misuse.

Reading in context protects believers from twisting promises, commands, warnings, or examples into meanings God did not intend. It helps teachers preach faithfully, Bible students study humbly, and ordinary believers understand more clearly what the Lord is saying.

The deepest context of Scripture is the unfolding plan of God fulfilled in Christ. Every passage should be handled according to its own meaning, yet the whole Bible moves toward the Savior, His kingdom, and His redeeming work.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Many people have been harmed by verses pulled out of context to control, shame, or manipulate them. Context helps restore trust by showing that God’s Word must be handled faithfully, not weaponized carelessly.

This also corrects shallow reading. A verse may encourage us, but true encouragement grows stronger when we understand what God actually meant in the passage.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: Before applying a verse, slow down and read what comes before and after it. Ask who is speaking, what is happening, what the passage means, and how it points to Christ. Let context guard your interpretation and deepen your obedience.
